opener: Lord, I keep looking at what's in my hand and calling it too small to matter.
paragraphs: I have the ordinary thing — the small idea, the little savings, the gift nobody's applauded yet, the one talent I've buried under "not now" and "not enough" — and I keep comparing it to the size of the need in front of me instead of bringing it to You. I've rehearsed every reason I'm not ready: not skilled enough, not backed enough, not far enough from my own failures to be trusted with anything that matters. So I wait. I keep the staff tucked under my arm instead of throwing it down where You can actually work with it.

But You never asked Moses for a resume — You asked him what was already in his hand, and You turned an old shepherd's stick into the rod of God the moment he stopped arguing and threw it down. So take what I've been embarrassed to call an offering, Lord. This isn't about what I lack, it's about who's holding it, and I'm done waiting for my hand to feel qualified before I open it to You. Not by might, nor by power, but by Your Spirit — do with what's already in my hand what my own strength never could. In Jesus' name, amen.
